base_member_text: [L90-L103, L208-L219] (MED/inconsistent-clamping) Manning friction is clamped to both mincf and maxcf at initialization but only to maxcf during updates, allowing the advertised lower bound to be lost after the first update.

[L248-L259] (MED/directional-inconsistency) The grain-size White-Colebrook update hard-caps cfu at the literal 0.1 while cfv uses par%maxcf, creating an unexplained directional difference and bypassing the configured u-direction cap.
audit_member_text: [L208-L219, L248-L269] (MED/limit-inconsistency) Update-time friction omits the initialization-time mincf lower clamp, and the grain-size u branch uniquely hard-caps at 0.1 instead of maxcf, producing direction- and timestep-dependent bounds.

adversarial.rationale: Comparing bedroughness_init with bedroughness_update confirms that the latter omits mincf and gives the grain-size U branch a different upper bound. The final maximum of 1 does not restore mincf or make the directional bounds equivalent.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex independent skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

base_member_text: [L198-L205] (LOW/division-precondition) Dynamic Manning roughness divides by dstem and droot with no local nonzero check, leaving its parameter contract implicit.
audit_member_text: [L196-L205] (HIGH/parameter-division) Dynamic Manning roughness divides by dstem and droot without requiring either configured length scale to be nonzero.

adversarial.rationale: The dynamic-roughness branches divide by dstem or droot, including the non-eroded branch when droot is zero. params.F90 accepts zero for both length scales, and neither the vegetation mask nor initialization supplies a positive substitute.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex independent skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

base_member_text: [L104-L164, L220-L272] (LOW/roughness-precondition) White-Colebrook formulas divide by kru/krv and take log10 without locally enforcing positive roughness heights, so validity depends entirely on upstream input constraints.
audit_member_text: [L70-L72, L104-L164, L220-L272] (HIGH/numerical-domain) Chezy and White-Colebrook formulas divide by unchecked bed-friction or roughness coefficients and take logarithms derived from them, allowing zero or nonpositive input to produce invalid coefficients.

adversarial.rationale: The coefficient-file read and the update formulas provide no nonzero/logarithm-domain validation for Chezy or White-Colebrook inputs. Scalar readkey bounds are warnings unless strict is requested, and a clamp after the division or logarithm cannot prevent its invalid evaluation.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex independent skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

base_member_text: [L196-L205] (MED/state-transition) After erosion sets isveggie false, subsequent calls fall through the unconditional elsewhere branch and can rebuild bedfriccoef from the original vegetated nman0, so the apparently permanent vegetation-removal state does not prevent roughness regrowth.

[L383-L397] (MED/boundary-value-inconsistency) For the last v row the interpolated infilb boundary is assigned directly from s%infil(:,s%ny) rather than copied from the adjacent interpolated v-point as done for the u boundary, producing an asymmetric boundary treatment.

[L690-L727] (LOW/staggered-variable-contract) Turbulence stresses use the signs of s%ue and s%ve while neighboring bed-stress code uses s%ueu and s%vev, leaving the intended staggered velocity/sign convention unclear.

audit_member_text: [L68-L165, L186-L273] (MED/selector-contract) Both bed-friction select blocks lack a default branch, so an unsupported selector leaves cfu and cfv unchanged or uninitialized without reporting an error.
dispositions.rationale: span-refuted: The normal parameter path restricts bedfriction to exactly the five handled selectors in params.F90 L683-L691 through parmapply. readkey.F90 L287-L312 rejects unsupported names and halts, so the absent default does not silently accept an unsupported user selector.

audit_member_text: [L78-L80, L105-L106, L147-L148, L320-L327, L438-L460, L547-L568, L686-L688] (HIGH/allocation-lifecycle) Saved work arrays are allocated without a module teardown or shape check, and several initialization allocations are unguarded, so repeated initialization or reuse at another grid size can fail or retain incompatible storage.

[L357-L378, L398-L418] (HIGH/numerical-domain) The infiltration enhancement divides by cfu or cfv twice without a positive lower-bound guard, which is unsafe for zero-valued constant-friction configurations.
dispositions.rationale: span-confirmed: The wet-face mask does not exclude zero friction: the CF initialization branch copies bedfriccoef directly, without a minimum. Infiltration enhancement then divides by cfu or cfv both in blphi and in the enhancement cap; the ventilation clamp does not protect either friction denominator.

audit_member_text: [L365-L373, L406-L414] (LOW/zero-input-bias) Exactly zero infiltration is forced to a nonzero negative blphi and therefore a facbl slightly different from one, so the nominally absent process still adds shear.
dispositions.rationale: span-confirmed: For zero infiltration and positive friction, blphi starts at zero but the nonnegative-infiltration branch replaces it with -1e-4. This gives facbl greater than one and a nonzero added shear for a flowing wet face with nonzero friction, even though infiltration is absent.

audit_member_text: [L476-L483, L570-L587, L596, L611] (HIGH/time-scale-division) Acceleration models divide by Trep-derived smoothing and frequency scales and by saved dt without validating Trep and dt as positive.

[L438-L460, L547-L568] (MED/shared-state-contract) The two acceleration implementations use the same allocation sentinel but allocate different array sets and initialize phirad only in one branch, so changing implementations during a process can expose unallocated or uninitialized saved state.
[L701-L727] (MED/directional-bias) Using SIGN with zero velocity assigns positive turbulent bed shear at rest, introducing a fixed directional bias wherever kbl is positive.
dispositions.rationale: span-confirmed: On a wet face with positive kbl and nonzero friction/turbulence coefficients, SIGN(1,0) contributes a positive shear even at zero velocity. Neither the wet mask nor the kbl test excludes that resting state.
